DP Type Level Transmitter Range Formulas at a Glance

A dp type level transmitter calculates liquid level from the hydrostatic head between its HP and LP ports. The HP side is connected to the bottom tapping and the LP side is vented in an open tank or connected to the tank top in a closed tank. Level is found from ΔP = H × SG, where H is the liquid height above the HP tap in mm and SG is the specific gravity of the process liquid.

LRV and URV Formula Table

Symbols: H = measuring span (mm), SG = process liquid SG, h = height of HP tap above the transmitter (mm), Hw = wet leg height (mm), SGw = wet leg fill SG. Results are in mmH2O.

InstallationLRV (0%)URV (100%)
Open tank, transmitter at HP tap0H × SG
Open tank, transmitter h below HP taph × SG(h + H) × SG
Closed tank, dry leg0H × SG
Closed tank, wet legminus Hw × SGwH × SG minus Hw × SGw
Closed tank, wet leg, transmitter h below HP taph × SG minus Hw × SGw(h + H) × SG minus Hw × SGw

Quick Check Example

For H = 2000 mm, SG = 1.1 and a 2500 mm wet leg filled with water (SGw = 1.0), the range is LRV = minus 2500 mmH2O and URV = 2200 minus 2500 = minus 300 mmH2O. The calibrated span is still 2200 mmH2O, because the wet leg only shifts the range and does not change the span.

Keep the wet leg completely full and the dry leg free of condensate, otherwise the zero will drift.
